Collingwood's AFLW horror season claims coach Sam Wright as player exodus and institutional turmoil rock the powerhouse club.
Evidence: 1 win from 11 games, captain Ruby Schleicher leaving, player unrest
#AFLW #Collingwood

Collingwood claims its AFLW program remains fully committed to driving forward despite the mounting losses and coaching departure.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Greater Good

Ground reality exposes acute structural failure, player departures, and deep staff frustration with list management and medical care.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.50, -1.80) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.2, z: 4)
Collingwood AFLW coach Sam Wright is stepping down after a dismal season with just one win, following captain Ruby Schleicher's departure to WA and widespread player unrest over club operations.

The Bright Side:
Clearing out failed management allows Collingwood to reset its AFLW program with accountable leadership and proper medical care.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The club confuses public PR optimism (Q4 Lyrical) with verifiable institutional performance and player welfare (Q3 Physical).

Social Physics Analysis:
Management ran a Smart Selfish Maneuver by masking internal dysfunction behind optimistic statements while players bore the physical and emotional burden of institutional neglect.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When institutional power promises flourishing ('will be') but delivers structural decay and administrative neglect ('is not'), it traces a destructive descent into failure.

The Unavoidable Truth: Elite club resources mean nothing without competent list management and genuine player care.

The Unavoidable Lie: PR spin can disguise a 1-win season and a mass player exodus.

Elite branding cannot substitute for competent governance; when institutions neglect their people, collapse follows.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to watch dedicated athletes and staff bear the heavy toll of administrative failure and institutional neglect.

Sam Wright will end his three-year stint as Collingwood AFLW coach at the end of this season. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Sarah Reed)

Collingwood's AFLW coach Sam Wright will leave his post at the end of the season.

The Magpies have already lost captain Ruby Schleicher, while there are reports of disharmony among players over list management, development coaching, and medical treatment.

Collingwood faces Essendon in the final round on Sunday, with both sides on the bottom of the ladder.

Collingwood's AFLW crisis has deepened, with coach Sam Wright another casualty in a horror season.

Wright will leave his position after the Magpies' final-round match against Essendon at Windy Hill on Sunday, ending a three-season campaign.

The Magpies have managed just one win from 11 games to anchor the AFLW ladder alongside the Bombers and St Kilda.

Former AFLW player and coach Lauren Arnell has criticised the standard of Collingwood, while emphasising the responsibility of coaches to "put on a show" to grow the game.

The match will also be the last for Essendon coach Natalie Wood, while St Kilda is already looking for a replacement for Nick Dal Santo.

Wright's news comes after skipper Ruby Schleicher announced last week she would leave the Magpies to head home to Western Australia, with other players believed to be also planning a departure.

Tarni White, Lauren Butler, Bri Davey, Sarah Rowe and Mattea Breed are all out of contract, while vice-captain Jordyn Allen is contracted but is expected to seek other opportunities.

Players and staff are reportedly frustrated with list management, development coaching, and medical treatment at the powerhouse AFL club.

Wright backed Collingwood's commitment to the women's football program.

"I look forward to coaching the group this Sunday and I wish them all the very best for the future — I leave knowing Collingwood is committed to driving its AFLW program forward," he said in a statement on Tuesday.

"It has been a privilege to serve the AFLW program at Collingwood.

"I will always look back on my time at the Pies with gratitude, and I want to thank every player, coach, staff member and supporter I've shared this journey with.

"While these decisions are never easy, I know it is the right one for my family and the football program as we move forward."

The Magpies haven't made the AFLW finals since 2022 when they were semifinalists, after ending the regular season sixth.

Despite their resources, they have finished outside the top 10 in each of the following seasons.
